title: Margins and return on capital
summary: Margins show how much of each dollar of revenue becomes profit. Return on capital = operating profit ÷ (debt + equity) shows how well all the money tied up in the business is used.
unreliableWhen: When margins are compared across very different industries, when one unusual year flatters the figures, or when return on equity looks high only because of heavy borrowing.
goodExample: A fictional food maker keeps its operating margin near 15% and its return on capital near 21% for three years.
badExample: A fictional office-machine maker's operating margin falls from 16% to under 11% and its return on capital drops to about 7%.
